subtopic: Parametric vs Non-Parametric Tests (t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney)
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #06: An online A/B experimentation platform detected anomalous metric movements and sample ratio mismatch (SRM) in Probability, Statistics & Hypothesis Testing. In an active experiment evaluating 'Parametric vs Non-Parametric Tests (t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney)', p-values were artificially deflated, and variance was underestimated by 60%.

### Engineering Challenge:
Which statistical remediation correctly eliminates false positive statistical significance in this 'Parametric vs Non-Parametric Tests (t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney)' evaluation?

options.text: Apply cluster-robust standard errors or Delta method variance corrections to account for intra-cluster correlation across repeated user sessions.
Run standard two-sample independent t-tests treating every individual page event as an independent observation.
Drop all users who logged in more than once during the experimental trial window.
Increase the alpha threshold from 0.05 to 0.20 to accept the observed metric variance.

answer_explanation: In Probability, Statistics & Hypothesis Testing, analyzing session-level observations when randomization occurs at the user level introduces intra-cluster correlation. Using naive standard errors severely underestimates variance. Cluster-robust variance estimators or the Delta method restore nominal false positive rates.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option A. Rationale: In Probability, Statistics & Hypothesis Testing, analyzing session-level observations when randomization occurs at the user level introduces intra-cluster correlation. Using naive standard errors severely underestimates variance. Cluster-robust variance estimators or the Delta method restore nominal false positive rates.
